chunks: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:

It was in the bequest of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) to his companions: 'Know that the Quran is a guidance for the day and a light for the dark night, upon whatever there may be of hardship and destitution.'

key_terms.جَهْد وَفَاقَة: Hardship and destitution — the physical and material difficulties of life that do not diminish the Quran's guidance
key_terms.نُورُ اللَّيْلِ الْمُظْلِمِ: Light of the dark night — the Quran as a source of light in times of confusion, hardship, and spiritual darkness
key_terms.هُدَى النَّهَارِ: Guidance of the day — the Quran as a clear, illuminating guide in times of clarity and ease
key_terms.وَصِيَّة: Wasiyya — a bequest or testament, the final counsel of a dying person or leader to those under their care; carries great moral weight in Islamic tradition

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the Quran as guidance in his bequest to his companions?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) transmits a testament of Imam Ali (AS) to his companions, declaring the Quran to be both a guiding light for the day and an illuminating beacon through the darkest nights of hardship and poverty. This saying comes from Imam Ali's wasiyya — his farewell counsel to his companions — emphasizing that the Quran's guidance is constant and unconditional, applicable regardless of the trials one faces. The original audience would have understood this as a call to remain firmly attached to the Quran even during the tribulations of early Islamic society.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Jameela who said, 
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said:

‘It was in the bequest of Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> to his<sup>asws</sup> companions: ‘Know that the Quran is a Guidance for the day, and light for the dark night, upon the one who was from a striving one and destitution’.
en.sarwar: Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from abu Jamilah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘It is in the will of Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) to his companions, “You must know that the Holy Quran is guidance during the day and light in the dark night against the existing hardships and poverty.”’
